candidates.name: GetTickCount64
verified_facts: Returns milliseconds elapsed since the system started
Its value is not adjusted by time-of-day clock corrections
semantic_limits: Elapsed boot time alone does not identify the canonical runner or prove receipt freshness.

candidates.name: QueryPerformanceCounter
verified_facts: Returns the current value of the high-resolution performance counter
Intervals require correlation with QueryPerformanceFrequency
semantic_limits: A counter value without frequency, process identity, and paired timestamps cannot prove event ordering.

candidates.name: QueryPerformanceFrequency
verified_facts: Returns the frequency of the high-resolution performance counter
The frequency is used to convert counter deltas into time intervals
semantic_limits: Frequency readback does not prove a measurement was captured on the intended host or process.

candidates.name: QueryUnbiasedInterruptTime
verified_facts: Returns unbiased interrupt time in 100-nanosecond units
Time spent in sleep or hibernation is excluded
semantic_limits: Unbiased time requires wall-clock and boot-session correlation before it can support receipt freshness.

candidates.name: QueryUnbiasedInterruptTimePrecise
verified_facts: Returns a more precise unbiased interrupt-time count
The count excludes sleep and hibernation time
semantic_limits: Precision does not establish authenticity, task ownership, or the exact producer of a receipt.

candidates.name: QueryInterruptTime
verified_facts: Returns the current interrupt-time count
The count can be compared with other boot-relative timing evidence
semantic_limits: Interrupt time alone cannot distinguish reboot, suspend, clock correction, or process replacement.

candidates.name: QueryInterruptTimePrecise
verified_facts: Returns a more precise interrupt-time count than QueryInterruptTime
The count is boot-relative rather than UTC
semantic_limits: A precise boot-relative count still requires machine, boot, process, and UTC correlation.

candidates.name: GetSystemTimePreciseAsFileTime
verified_facts: Returns current UTC system date and time as a FILETIME
It provides the highest available system-time precision
semantic_limits: Wall-clock time can be adjusted and therefore cannot be the sole freshness or ordering proof.

candidates.name: GetSystemTimeAdjustmentPrecise
verified_facts: Returns precise clock adjustment parameters
The values describe how the time-of-day clock is being adjusted
semantic_limits: Adjustment parameters do not prove synchronization quality or receipt producer identity.

candidates.name: Time Functions
verified_facts: Indexes Windows time-of-day, performance-counter, interrupt-time, and conversion functions
Different APIs have different sleep and adjustment semantics
semantic_limits: An API index is documentation evidence only and does not prove any F-host call occurred.

candidates.name: GetSystemPowerStatus
verified_facts: Retrieves AC-line, battery, charging, and power-saving status
Failure details are available through GetLastError
semantic_limits: Power status is a point-in-time observation and cannot prove uninterrupted runner execution.

candidates.name: SYSTEM_POWER_STATUS
verified_facts: Defines fields returned for AC line, battery state, remaining life, and power-saving status
Unknown values are explicitly representable
semantic_limits: A populated structure does not prove the values were captured on the intended F-host.

candidates.name: PowerGetActiveScheme
verified_facts: Returns the GUID of the active power scheme
The returned buffer is allocated for the caller
semantic_limits: The active scheme does not prove whether sleep, hibernation, or throttling occurred during the attempt.
